tatuaje--tatuaje-brown-label-miami-selec.description: The Seleccion de Cazador, known as the Brown Label or Miami line, is where Tatuaje began in 2003, when Pete Johnson joined forces with Pepín García. Nicaraguan binder and filler sit under an Ecuador Habano wrapper. Baking spice and pepper lead, then the smoke turns nutty and cedary before an earthy, faintly creamy close.

thirds.notes: Cinnamon, nutmeg and a brown-sugar sweetness open, with pepper rising on the retrohale.
Sweetness recedes; a nutty core with light cedar sits under steady pepper.
The nuts sharpen, a soft creaminess appears and the finish settles into earth.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Seleccion de Cazador Regios review

tatuaje--tatuaje-reserva.description: The Reserva sizes extend the Seleccion de Cazador range with Nicaraguan binder and filler, aiming for a softer edge and more layers than the Miami blend; later runs such as the 7th Reserva and Cojonu 2012 add Sumatra and broadleaf versions. Molasses and cocoa sweetness give way to espresso, wood and a leathery end.

thirds.notes: The early spice fades into a molasses-like sweetness with floral honey and flashes of chocolate.
Spice returns, cocoa and espresso grow, and the smoke turns drier with a woody edge.
Espresso leads with savoury wood, lingering spice and a firm leather note at the end.

sources.title: Stogie Review – Tatuaje J21 guest review

tatuaje--tatuaje-broadleaf-reserva-broad.description: First shown in 2016 as the Reserva Broadleaf Collection, this line dresses the classic Brown Label sizes in a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled at My Father Cigars. It opens on leather, earth and espresso with pepper, then turns to cinnamon, dark chocolate and a gentle vanilla sweetness.

thirds.notes: Firm leather and gritty earth with espresso, a floral hint and plenty of black pepper on the retrohale.
Cinnamon and earth take the lead with dark chocolate and hay, as vanilla replaces the floral note.
Cinnamon and earth stay central; vanilla grows, with passing cocoa, leather and cedar.

sources.title: halfwheel – Tatuaje Tainos Reserva Broadleaf review

tatuaje--tatuaje-black.description: Tatuaje Black is a Nicaraguan puro under a sun-grown criollo wrapper, made at My Father Cigars in Estelí and brought back in 2013 for the brand's tenth year. Pepper and a sweet citrus note open, then creamy cocoa and grapefruit fill out a balanced, oily smoke that stays lively to the end.

thirds.notes: Pepper on the retrohale without heat, with sweet citrus and a touch of earth.
The blend settles: grapefruit and creamy cocoa join the pepper, leaving an oily feel on the palate.
Flavours deepen to peppery grapefruit and cocoa with a toasted, graham-like sweetness.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – Tatuaje Black Label Corona Gorda review

tatuaje--tatuaje-havana-vi.description: Havana VI pairs an Ecuador Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler, offered in sizes from the Angeles to the Nobles robusto and a lancero. Pepper and dark cherry open over leather, then wood, baking spice and a little coffee take over in a creamy, medium-strength smoke that suits an afternoon.

thirds.notes: Pepper first, then dark cherry and leather in a smooth, creamy smoke.
Wood and leather lead with warm baking spice, cedar and a light coffee note.
Wood steps forward with a bourbon-barrel character over the leather core; a slight bitterness may build.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Tatuaje Havana VI Nobles

tatuaje--tatuaje-havana-vi-verocu.description: Verocu is rolled in Nicaragua from Nicaraguan binder and filler under an Ecuador wrapper, finished with a Cuban triple cap and blended in a medium-bodied Cuban style; it became a line of its own in 2015. Sweet leather, wood and nuts open with spice, then cocoa and black coffee arrive before leather leads the finish.

thirds.notes: Sweet leather, wood and nuts, with a spice that fills the palate.
The profile holds steady while cocoa and black coffee come through.
Leather takes over, backed by peppery spice and toasted nuts.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Tatuaje Verocu No. 2 review

tatuaje--tatuaje-havana-vi-verocu-blue.description: Launched in 2022, Verocu Blue is a Nicaraguan puro from the My Father factory, with Nicaraguan binder and filler under an oily, dark Nicaraguan wrapper. Hazelnut, a cappuccino-like creaminess and leather lead a smooth, balanced smoke, with black pepper and herbal notes arriving late.

thirds.notes: Creamy and nutty from the start, with hazelnut, cappuccino and leather over light spice.
The same profile with a fuller aroma.
Black pepper becomes the main spice and a herbal note joins in.

sources.title: Holt's – Tatuaje Havana VI Verocu Blue
Cigars Lover – Tatuaje Havana VI Verocú Blue No. 2

tatuaje--tatuaje-serie-p.description: Serie P is Tatuaje's everyday cigar, a Nicaraguan-filled blend that returned in 2011 under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, in robusto, short robusto and toro sizes. It smokes mellow and even, moving from leather and wood to a buttered-bread note and natural tobacco near the end, a fit for a relaxed daytime break.

thirds.notes: Leather with a small zing, then wood and a hint of buttered bread.
Leather drops back and wood leads; the smoke turns a little drier.
Bread and butter with natural tobacco and a dry finish in the last inch.

sources.title: Stogie Review – Tatuaje Series P 2011 version

tatuaje--tatuaje-negociant-monopole.description: Named after the wine trade's négociant, who blends grapes bought from other growers, Monopole uses tobacco from My Father Cigars: an Ecuador shade wrapper over Mexican and Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is gentler than most Tatuaje, buttery with cashew and cedar, then apricot sweetness and white pepper.

thirds.notes: A light pepper, then a buttery smoothness with cashew and plenty of cedar.
A sweetness like apricot takes shape over the continuing nuttiness.
White pepper comes forward on the retrohale, with nuts, earth and cedar on the finish.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Tatuaje Negociant Monopole #1 review

tatuaje--tatuaje-hcs.description: The HCS line sets an Ecuador Habano wrapper over aged Nicaraguan long filler in three sizes, from the No. 1 Robusto Larga to the No. 3 Torpedo Cubano. Expect a full-strength smoke built on pepper, cedar, leather and earth, best kept for the end of a meal.

tatuaje--tatuaje-hcs-maduro.description: The maduro version of the HCS line swaps the Ecuador Habano wrapper for dark Connecticut broadleaf over aged Nicaraguan long filler. It comes in a single size, the No. 1 Robusto Larga, and smokes at full strength. It is the darker counterpart to the Habano-wrapped HCS, for smokers who prefer broadleaf.

thirds.notes: Cocoa and sweetness with an early black-pepper punch that soon softens, and cedar emerging.
Bittersweet baking cocoa and sweeter cedar, balanced by a growing creaminess.
Cream leads with sweet cocoa, and a citrus note adds a slight tartness.

tatuaje--tatuaje-corojo.description: The Corojo sizes, including the T110 short robusto, revisit Pete Johnson's early high-strength blend: a Nicaraguan corojo wrapper grown by the García family over ligero-heavy Nicaraguan filler, made at My Father Cigars in Estelí. The power arrives early, with pepper and earth, then cocoa, coffee and wood bring some sweetness.

tatuaje--tatuaje-10th-anniversary.description: Made for the brand's tenth year in 2013, the 10th Anniversary uses a Cuban-seed Habano wrapper grown in Ecuador over aged Nicaraguan long filler, in a perfecto and a robusto. It is a full, rich smoke with leather, cinnamon, cocoa and woody notes, made for a slow evening.

sources.title: Cigars Lover – Tatuaje 10th Anniversary Capa Especial

tatuaje--tatuaje-10th-anniversary-capa-e.description: In 2024 Tatuaje returned to its 10th Anniversary sizes with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, which it calls Capa Especial, over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The limited run comprised 3,000 boxes each of the Belle Encre perfecto and the Bon Chasseur, both 5 3/8 inches long.

sources.title: Cigars Lover – Tatuaje 10th Anniversary Capa Especial

tatuaje--tatuaje-15th-anniversary-oscuro.description: Released in 2018, the 15th Anniversary Oscuro revives a blend Pete Johnson and Pepín García first made for the Grand Havana Room in the mid-2000s: a dark Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled at El Rey de los Habanos in Miami. Pepper and cedar open, leather builds, and a creamy, chocolate finish follows.

thirds.notes: A burst of pepper with cedar, a tea-like note, light earth and dry leather.
Pepper and meaty leather at first, softening into cedar sweetness and some roasted coffee.
Creamy and slightly sweet, with spiced chocolate, leather and black pepper at the end.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Tatuaje 15th Anniversary Habano Oscuro

tatuaje--tatuaje-15th-anniversary-rosado.description: The Rosado is the lighter-wrapped partner of the 15th Anniversary Oscuro, both released in 2018 as revivals of blends first made for the Grand Havana Room in the mid-2000s. An Ecuadorian wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled at El Rey de los Habanos in Miami, in belicoso and torpedo sizes.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Tatuaje 15th Anniversary (release background)

tatuaje--tatuaje-20th-anniversary.description: Shipped in October 2023 for the brand's twentieth year, this limited blend is rolled in Estelí with an Ecuadorian wrapper, a double Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan filler. Milk chocolate, vanilla and black cherry open, a smoky leather middle follows, and cedar, almond and honey close a smoke that softens towards the end.

thirds.notes: Sweet from the first puff: milk chocolate, vanilla and black cherry over damp earth and black coffee.
A smoky, fire-cured turn with leather and graham cracker, and pepper kept in the background.
Cedar, almond and honey lead as the cigar mellows and leather returns near the end.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Tatuaje 20th Anniversary Grand Chasseur

tatuaje--tatuaje-el-triunfador-original.description: El Triunfador began in 2008 as a 7 1/2 x 38 lancero that Pete Johnson made largely to secure the old Cuban brand name; a full line followed a year later. A Connecticut broadleaf wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler. Coffee, cedar and orange open, then cocoa, peanut and earth, with sweetness and wood at the close.

thirds.notes: Coffee and cedar lead, with orange peel, leather and a salty edge on the finish.
Cocoa, toast, peanut and sweet earth, set against herbal spice and a little white pepper.
Sweetness peaks with herbs and spice; cedar and oak add wood to the finish.

sources.title: halfwheel – Tatuaje El Triunfador Lancero Original review

tatuaje--tatuaje-nuevitas.description: Nuevitas Estelí, released in July 2018, is a Nicaraguan puro wrapped in Nicaraguan 99 leaf and made at My Father Cigars. It starts sweet and creamy with coffee, white pepper and baking spice, then charred oak, earth and leather, and finishes with semi-sweet chocolate, toasted nuts and strong black pepper.

thirds.notes: Sweet and creamy with coffee, white pepper and baking spice, plus meaty wood and char.
Pepper builds alongside charred oak and earth, with a leathery finish and a mineral note.
Semi-sweet chocolate joins the woody base, with toasted nuts, earth and firm black pepper.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Tatuaje Nuevitas Estelí

tatuaje--tatuaje-nuevitas-jibaro.description: Jibaro, Spanish for a poor country farmer, is an older Pete Johnson blend brought back around 2020 and now made at My Father Cigars as a Nicaraguan puro under a Corojo '99 wrapper. After a rough start it settles into pepper and coffee, then cream and cocoa, with a light bitter edge late on.

thirds.notes: An unsettled opening gives way to mild pepper and coffee.
Coffee grows as pepper recedes, joined by cream, cocoa and a light spice.
The coffee, cocoa and cream profile holds, with a mild hoppy bitterness.

sources.title: Stogie Press – Tatuaje Nuevitas Jibaro No. 1 review

tatuaje--tattoo.description: Tattoo was created to protect the brand's English name, first as a small annual run of box-pressed lanceros, now joined by the Caballero robusto. A dark Habano Rosado wrapper from Ecuador covers Nicaraguan binder and filler from My Father Cigars. Powdered cocoa and cedar open, then earth, herbs and pepper take over.

thirds.notes: Dry cocoa and cedar with a general sweetness; pepper can push to the front.
Cocoa and pepper soften, letting earth, cedar and herbs come through.
Cocoa fades; earth and cedar dominate with more herbs and a peppery finish.

tatuaje--fausto.description: Fausto is Tatuaje's heavyweight: an Ecuadorian Habano maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and ligero-rich filler from Estelí and Jalapa, with the yearly Avion perfecto released since 2011. Dark earth, cocoa and pepper lead, roasted coffee and toasted wood follow, and the strength rises to full in the last third.

thirds.notes: Dark earth and cocoa with lingering spice; cedar and pepper on the retrohale.
The smoke turns toasty, with roasted coffee and charred wood beside the cocoa and a hint of sweetness.
A slight tartness appears while cocoa, earth and pepper stay in balance.

sources.title: Casas Fumando – Tatuaje Fausto Avion 12 review

tatuaje--tatuaje-skinny-monsters.description: Skinny Monsters are a slim Halloween-themed line, mostly 6 x 38, made with Pepín García and following the earlier Little and Pudgy Monsters. Ten blends exist, each with its own character and strength, sold in boxes of one blend or in Lancero and Cazadores Edition boxes holding one of each.

tatuaje--my-father-tatuaje-la-union.description: La Union marks more than twenty years of shared history between Tatuaje and My Father Cigars, with each house making a cigar for the other. Released in a single Prominente Especial size, it comes in versions under an Ecuador Sumatra or a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper, at full strength.

sources.title: Holt's – My Father & Tatuaje La Union
halfwheel – La Union, Tatuaje for My Father
